#2465. La réserve renverse Le Cannet-Rocheville sous les yeux de Lopez

Sous les yeux de Christian Lopez, qui a donné le coup d'envoi fictif de cette rencontre entre ses deux anciens clubs, la réserve s'est imposée (2-1) ce samedi sur le fil et sur le terrain du Cannet-Rocheville (Alpes Maritimes) grâce à un renversant doublé de Lamine Sonko (photo).

Après un premier quart d'heure plutôt équilibré, l'ASSE a pris l'ascendant mais n'a pas su ouvrir le score malgré deux grosses occasions de son très remuant ailier gauche Etienne Mendy et une tentative de Mamadou Konté sauvée in extremis sur sa ligne par un défenseur.

Sainté a concédé l'ouverture du score à la 56e minute suite à un 6 mètres joué trop vite suivi d'une perte de balle. Les Maralpins ont bien joué le coup sur cette action qui semblait quand même entachée d'une légère faute sur Mamadou Konté.

Boostés par l'apport de leurs entrants, les Verts ont égalisé à la 86e minute sur une ouverture de leur latéral droit Tom Teillol pour Lamine Sonko, qui a résisté au retour de deux défenseurs avant de mettre un petit piqué pour tromper le mal prénommé mais bien nommé Victor Battu.

A la 92e minute, Nathan Kasia a perdu le ballon mais s'est bagarré pour le récupérer et lancer Noah Moulin, dont le centre tendu a été repris victorieusement par le supersub Lamine Sonko. Ce succès permet aux Verts de monter provisoirement à la 2e place du classement, derrière le solide leader Berre.

La compo : Colombet - Teillol, Gueye, Kasia, Lenou - Depalle (Thouilleux, 82'), Rised, Reynaud (Cheikh, 75')- Toty, Konte (Sonko, 68'), Mendy 'Moulin, 68')

La réaction de Sylvain Gibert : "On a su faire la différence à la fin du match mais on aurait mérité de mener au score à la pause car la dernière demi-heure de la première période a été très bonne. On a manqué d'efficacité devant le but, c'est donc notre adversaire qui a ouvert le score. Mais on est reparti de l'avant, on a insisté et au final on a été récompensé. C'est la victoire de tout un groupe, les entrants notamment nous ont apporté l'énergie nécessaire pour renverser ce match. Les joueus étaient venus ici pour gagner et ils se sont donnés les moyens d'y parvenir. Il faut les féliciter pour ça. On est content d'avoir décroché ce succès sous les yeux de Christian Lopez, qui nous a fait l'honneur d'être présent et d'échanger avec nous à la fin du match. C'était top car c'est un joueur que j'ai cité la saison dernière dans mes causeries. Je trouve qu'il représente les valeurs du club, cette capacité à ne jamais renoncer, comme l'illustre son mythique intervention sur Oleg Blokhine contre Kiev."

#2462. European Roundup: Maiden goals for Wirtz, Goretzka and Woltemade

Leon Goretzka and Nick Woltemade scored their first league goals for their new clubs, while Florian Wirtz ended his goal drought at Liverpool.

It took him until matchday 10, but Wirtz finally scored his first Premier League goal of the season in Liverpool's 3-1 win at bottom-placed Crystal Palace. The Germany international also set up ex-Borussia Dortmund striker Alexander Isak for the third goal as he already has the same number of assists (3) to his entire first season in England's top-flight.

Liverpool's win helped Manchester United to not further slip in the standings after their roller-coaster draw at home against Aston Villa. In a game three former Bayern players were on target, Noussair Mazraoui registered only his second assist in Manchester United colors.

The visitors led by a two-goal margin twice before having to settle for a draw. Nicolas Jackson continued his excellent form in front of goal, while Joshua Zirkzee got his first league goal of the season. Former Germany international Goretzka also scored his first-ever Premier League goal in his second start before Michael Carrick's side climbed to 18th place with two extra-time goals.

At the other end of the table, Fabian Hürzeler's Brighton are now up to second in the standings after Manchester City's third defeat in the row. Daniel Farke's Leeds United and Marco Rose's Bournemouth also prevailed before the break, while Matthias Jaissle's job is in danger at Newcastle United as they have only won once from the last six games in all competitions.

Newcastle United loanee Nick Woltemade is now in a good run of form for Juventus, despite Jürgen Klopp's snub for Germany's November games. The 24-year-old failed to score for the first time in Europe when his club returned home from Alkmaar with three points on Thursday, but he finally netted his first Serie A goal when the former giants had to settle for a hard-fought point in Florence.

Derby della Madonnina hero Christian Pulisic scored in each of his last three Serie A starts as the latest goal by the ex-BVB man helped AC Milan to a narrow win at in-form Genoa. Meanwhile, Inter recovered immediately as Marcus Thuram's goal in the 2-0 win over Como helped him reach 50 goals in domestic competitions since leaving Borussia Mönchengladbach on a free transfer.

Former Bundesliga center-backs Arthur Theate and Mario Hermoso were also on target in matchday 11 Serie A action for Bologna and AS Roma, respectively.

Marc Bartra is another ex-Bundesliga center-half to score this weekend after he was an unused substitute in his return to Westfalenstadion. The 35-year-old found the net in back-to-back league games for LaLiga outfit Real Betis for the first time since December 2019.

After a difficult season in England with Everton, Adam Aznou is trying to find his feet in Spain with Malaga, where he joined on an initial loan deal. However, he will now face more time on the sidelines after his red card in their 2-1 defeat to fellow newly-promoted side Racing Santander.

Saturday's clash was the first time the former FC Bayern youngster started a home league game since leaving the Rekordmeister on bad terms. Elsewhere in LaLiga, former Augsburg attacker Ruben Vargas missed a first-half penalty-kick in Sevilla’s goalless draw with out-of-form Alaves.

Yan Diomandè’s Real Madrid are now in second place in Spanish's top-flight after Barcelona ended Atlético Madrid's seven-game winning streak as Hansi Flick's men extend their lead at the top. In France, PSG head into the break with 11 successive wins in all competitions.

Paris Brunner's AS Monaco are now dropped to seventh place as a 1-1 draw at newcomers Le Mans extended their winless run to five games. Nice and Brest continued their good forms as Jonathan Clauss and Ludovic Ajourque continued their scoring run. Gio Reyna reached three league goals for the first time since the 2022/23 season, although Strasbourg have lost five of their last six Ligue 1 encounters.

Reyna's ex-teammate Julian Brandt missed Ajax's last two games due to an injury. The record Eredivisie winners had a chance to climb to the top of the table after Feyenoord's 5-3 defeat at Heerenveen. However, they squandered a two-goal lead against Twente as former Wolfsburg and Hoffenheim striker Wout Weghorst beat Germany's number one Marc-André ter Stegen with a 95th-minute penalty-kick.

The top five teams in Eredivisie are only separated by three points as Peter Bosz's PSV are now back in top place following a 5-2 win at newcomers Cambuur.

Thomas Reis’ winning streak at Trabzonspor ended on Thursday by SC Freiburg, but he still has a perfect record in Süper Lig as Mohamed Salah's goal helped his side to climb past Amedspor in second place. Hoffenheim loanee Gift Orban has scored more goals than compatriot Victor Osimhen and Salah, but the debutants dropped to third after a 4-3 defeat at league leaders Galatasaray.

Meanwhile, Bayer Leverkusen loanee Ernest Poku scored his first league goal for Beşiktaş. Former Germany youth international Davie Selke was also on target on matchday 11 of Turkish top-flight for İstanbul Başakşehir.

Ex-Ingolstadt man Dennis Eckert scored a hat-trick for St. Liege to help the former giants beat Beveren in Belgian Pro League. RB Salzburg extended their winning streak in Austrian Bundesliga to four games with a 4-3 victory over Sturm Graz as Haris Tabaković, Leandro Morgalla and Jesper Lindstrøm were all on target.

Former VfB Stuttgart and Hertha BSC midfielder Santiago Ascacibar won the revamped Argentine Campeón de Liga in a dramatic manner with Boca Juniors. The giants squeezed past Rosario Central with Enner Valencia’s 96th-minute winner against Defensa y Justicia.

#2460. PSV hold on to book narrow Champions League win in Porto

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

PSV survived a second-half onslaught in Porto to secure their first win of the Champions League group stages.

Guus Til scored the only goal when he tapped in from close range after Esmir Bajraktarevic’s shot had come back off the post and was steered across goal by Sven Mijnans.

The Eindhoven club were worth their narrow lead against Francesco Farioli’s side after dominating possession in the first half, but rarely troubled Diogo Costa in the Porto goal.

Til went close with a header early in the second half before putting PSV ahead in the 57th minute.

But the visitors had to defend heroically as Porto poured forward in search of an equaliser, aided by an increasingly fragile Matej Kovar.

The goalkeeper put his defenders in jeopardy with a weak clearance in the 72nd minute, but redeemed himself by saving Victor Froholdt’s shot with his chest before Lutsarel Geertruida blocked the follow-up from Pepê.

A minute later Kovar was left stranded after he rushed out of his penalty area, but Sergiño Dest managed to hack the ball away before Alberto Costa could poke it into the open goal.

At the other end, substitute Denis Man came close to scoring a second for PSV with his first touch when his curling shot beat Costa but failed to sneak inside the post.

The 1-0 win lifts PSV to a provisional 16th place in the Champions League table at the halfway stage of round three, while Porto are still looking for their first point.

Their next match is at home to Belgian side Club Brugge, who will make the short trip to Eindhoven on November 4.

#2459. "I'm involved in 50 percent of his goals" – Hoeneß makes bold Karl claim after criticism

Bayern Munich honorary president Uli Hoeneß made headlines just over two weeks ago when he criticised youngster Lennart Karl for lacking humility and revealed plans to have a serious conversation with the teenager following a dip in performances.

Since then, the 18-year-old has stepped up his performances, most recently scoring the winning goals in Bayern's 2-0 victory over Atletico Madrid and 2-1 win against Mainz.

Speaking on BR's Sonntags-Stammtisch programme on Sunday, Hoeneß jokingly suggested that Karl's upturn in form since his criticism is no coincidence.

"I'm involved in 50 percent of his goals," Hoeneß said with a smile, adding that he sees it as his responsibility to guide young players.

“We have a duty to show young players the way,” he added.

"I have so much experience. But if a young player doesn't listen to me, then I have to stop."

In his criticism of Karl, Hoeneß took aim at the youngster's use of social media, reflecting his wider concerns about its influence on young players.

"Social media is the biggest problem," he said, describing the world of influencers as a "cesspit".

The Bayern honorary president believes young players, in particular, can quickly lose sight of what really matters amid the constant attention and self-promotion on social media.

“I have to do something about that. I also see it as my responsibility to speak out,” he underlined.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Feyenoord endured a frustrating evening in Spain as a penalty by Real Betis’s outstanding player, Isco, secured a 1-0 win for the La Liga side.

The Rotterdammers were second best for most of the game, but held out until the 59th minute, when Abde Ezzalzouli’s cross hit the arm of Jeremiah St. Juste in front of goal.

Isco, who was at the heart of Betis’s attacks all evening, grabbed the ball and gave Tjark Ernst no chance from the penalty spot.

Ernst had made good saves from former AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott and Marc Batra to keep Feyenoord in the game in the first half, but Feyenoord had the best chance of the opening period when Gjivai Zechiël shot over the bar from close range.

The visitors had a claim for a penalty of their own turned down in the 68th minute when Givairo Read claimed he had been pushed by Ezzalzouli, but referee Simone Sozza waved the appeals away.

The result leaves Giovanni van Bronckhorst’s side in 26th place in the Champions League table, with Internazionale up next in De Kuip on November 3.

#2447. Houdayer chatouillé

Les Verts ont parfaitement suivi notre mot d'ordre en ayant mis hier soir sous l'éteignoir Mathys Houdayer, comme le souligne aujourd'hui Ouest-France.

"Le buteur tango a évolué en n°10, et a commencé par devoir défendre. Identifié et ciblé offensivement, il a eu droit à un traitement de faveur, en subissant quelques tacles appuyés, en étant serré de près. Il a pris dans la foulée un jaune pour contestation (24’). Souvent touché dos au jeu, il y a éprouvé des difficultés. Il a loupé des choses très simples, frustré. Cela fait partie de l’apprentissage d’un jeune joueur. Il n’a toutefois pas abdiqué, mais a loupé ce test chez le leader. "Il faut qu’il s’aguerrisse. Il a été un peu chatouillé, serré de près. Avec ce qu’il fait depuis le début de la saison, il est logique qu’il soit surveillé" a déclaré David Vignes.

Mais c'est un attaquant tango prêté par Monaco qui prend le plus gros tacle et se voit décerner la plus mauvaise note (2/10) par le quotidien régional.

"Aligné devant en l’absence de Trévis Dago et Abou Kanté, Ouma Konaté n’a pas existé hier. Il n’a rien montré, hormis quelques velléités de pressing. Il a été régulièrement dominé dans les duels, physiquement. Et c’est lui qui perd dans ce domaine le ballon qui se termine en 1-0. Entré en jeu à Nancy, où il avait loupé une grosse occasion, blessé face à Boulogne, Konaté semble loin du compte. "On a manqué de poids, on ne résiste pas au duel. Les absences ont pesé lourd, c'est insuffisant" déplore le coach lavallois."

#2442. Hertha beat their ex-captain in front of 70,000 fans, Bielefeld and Magdeburg cruising – 5 things we learned from 2. Bundesliga Matchday 11

Hertha BSC’s healthy lead at the top of 2. Bundesliga continues after a hard-fought win over Wolfsburg on matchday 11.

70,000 fans were in attendance for Hertha BSC’s narrow win over fellow promotion hopefuls VfL Wolfsburg in the last 2. Bundesliga Topspiel before the season's second international break. After Cleiton’s early red card, the league leaders scored two goals at the end of the first-half, but they had a difficult time after the restart as Tobias Strobl’s men halved the deficit almost immediately.

However, Hertha still managed to take all three points as they only dropped two points after 11 rounds. Stefan Leitl's side weren't one of the pre-season favorites after the departures of key players, but they're now ten points ahead of third-placed Kaiserslautern.

Fabian Reese is one of the star players who left Hertha in the summer, but he was unable to make an impact on his return to a packed Olympiastadion. It was only the third time that the former Hertha captain didn't register a direct goal contribution in Wolfsburg colors.

Nürnberg and Kaiserslautern will spend the international break in the top three after their respective wins over Darmstadt and Osnabrück. Miroslav Klose's men scored two second-half goals to return to winning ways at Max-Morlock-Stadion against relegation-threatened Darmstadt.

Meanwhile, Kaiserslautern's robust defense recovered from conceding three goals to all-conquering Hertha by keeping their eighth clean sheet of the season to help Torsten Lieberknecht's side record another narrow victory. Nürnberg and Kaiserslautern will host bottom half teams Eintracht Braunschweig and Dynamo Dresden after the international break.

Sixth time lucky: Bochum finally win at home

Uwe Rösler's troops are in a good run of form as they won three games on the trot. After qualifying for the Round of 16 in DFB-Pokal, Bochum won back-to-back games in 2. Bundesliga against Energie Cottbus and Karlsruher SC.

Sunday's late win against Karlsruhe ended their long wait for a first home win. The club's top-scorer Philipp Hofmann scored a second-half brace, including the winning goal in injury-time. The former Karlsruhe striker found the net in each of the last three games for VfL.

Arminia Bielefeld are another team in excellent form as they climbed out of the relegation zone with four wins in their last five games. Following their Saturday's success in Kiel, Oliver Kirch’s men climbed to sixth place with 17 points.

Meanwhile, Kiel are bottom of the 2. Bundesliga as Tim Walter's side lost back-to-back games for the first time. The former HSV, Stuttgart and Hull City coach is a candidate for the second managerial casualty in the league after Hannover replaced Christian Titz with Sandro Wagner.

One team that quickly sorted out their issues is certainly Magdeburg. After starting the season with a 6-1 home defeat to Braunschweig, Magdeburg collected 20 points in their last 10 games. A 4-1 victory over last season's Bundesliga club St. Pauli lifted the modest club to fourth place as they even lead the home table alongside Hertha.

#2441. Bosz frustrated as Feyenoord hold PSV to 1-1 draw in Eindhoven

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Feyenoord preserved their four-point advantage over champions PSV after coming away with a point from Eindhoven thanks to an improved second-half performance.

PSV dominated the first half as they deployed a close-passing, tiki-taka style to stifle Feyenoord, but only had Guus Til’s well-taken volley after 20 minutes to show for it.

Ten minutes after the break Feyenoord equalised when Anis Hadj Moussa was given too much space to charge down the right flank and bend a shot inside the far post.

The Algerian had a good chance for a second towards the end, while PSV goalkeeper Matej Kovar had to be alert to keep out a header by Nacho Ferri from close range.

“We were by far the better team today and had the better chances,” said PSV coach Peter Bosz. “We started the second half badly and made a mistake, after which Hadj Moussa scored. And even then we could have won it.”

Ajax overtook PSV to close the gap at the top to three points with a hard-fought win at Sparta. Veteran striker Jens Toornstra scored for Sparta on his 500th Eredivisie appearance, but Abdellah Ouazane and Tolu Arokodare, the scorers against Atalanta in midweek, were on target again to claim the win for Ajax.

Twente moved up to fourth place as two late goals by Sondre Ørjasæter and Lucas Vennegoor of Hesselink earned a 2-0 win at AZ Alkmaar, who like Twente and PSV have 20 points.

Fortuna Sittard also snatched the points late on against Excelsior as Rodrigo Guth headed in a corner in injury time to keep the Limburg club in sixth place, two points further back.

At the other end of the table, the return of Adrie Koster as veteran coach brought no relief to Willem II, who crashed to a 6-1 home defeat to Cambuur.

The Tilburgers remain four points behind ADO Den Haag, who were unable to keep up the momentum of last week’s win against PSV as they lost 3-2 at home to Heerenveen.

Telstar lost by the same margin at Go Ahead Eagles, whose striker Søren Tengstedt netted twice in the first half to lead the Eredivisie scoring charts with eight goals.

Are you the most knowledgeable football fan around? Do you want to be involved with EA SPORTS FIFA? Well, you’re in luck as the FIFA Talent Scout team is looking for people like you.

The FIFA Talent Scout community has over 6000 active members and is always looking for individuals to help improve their football database.

This is a great opportunity to put your knowledge of your club to good use, helping to ensure that the EA SPORTS football database continues to contain the most up to date and accurate team and player data for the many leagues featured in FIFA 17.

The first step into our community is as a football analyst, who can examine team and player data and offer feedback suggesting possible changes. You can contribute towards improving player appearance, player attributes, team formations and team tactics. There is no minimum or maximum expectation in terms of your contribution to the database. The key is that when you do contribute, your feedback helps to improve the authenticity of FIFA 17.

Those who stand out may be offered the chance to join our editing team and the chance to take full responsibility for a team and its squad. #2438. La situation se corse pour les U19

Mal en point(s) les U19 Stéphanois (7 points en 9 rencontres) se déplaçaient en Corse ce matin pour y affronter Bastia, 3 points de plus au compteur. Un peu rassurés après les promesses entrevues face à Monaco (1-2), les protégés de Frédéric Dugand ont à nouveau affiché leurs limites, s'inclinant à nouveau (c'est la 4ème fois) sur le score de 0-3 !

En première période, la possession est verte, mais de façon stérile. Les Stéphanois sont maladroits et rejoignent la mi-temps sans le moindre tir cadré ! En face, Bastia va de son côté être très réaliste et  tromper à 2 reprises, sur autant d’occasions, le portier vert Lorik Vial, aux 40ème et 44ème minutes. (Bastia 2  ASSE 0 ; mi-temps).

En seconde période les Verts ne sont pas plus inspirés, avec une seule occasion, une tentative de Fousseny Sidibé Kaloga bien stoppé par le gardien Bastiais. La fin de match tourne au cauchemar, avec un rouge récolté par ce même Fousseny Kaloga et un troisième pion encaissé sur la 3ème tentative corse (90ème) ! (Bastia 3  ASSE 0 ; score final).

Avec cette 5ème défaite consécutive (la 7ème au total), les jeunes Verts sont dorénavant avant derniers et relégables, seul Borgo (1 point) faisant moins bien qu’eux. Une réaction est attendue et obligatoire la semaine prchaine, avec la réception de l'US Cap d'Ail, 12 points, auteur d'un nul aujourd'hui face à Balma (2-2).

La Composition : Vial – Akil (Demassieux 70ème), E.Mnemoi, Assoumani (Lengi 46ème), Jolivet, Marliac, N.Mouton, O.Mendy, Kaloga, Zibi, Vibert (Gobé 62ème).

La réaction de Frédéric Dugand : « Il nous a manqué de tout. De la justesse technique, de la justesse dans nos choix défensifs comme offensifs. On ne peut pas rivaliser si on ne montre pas plus de caractère pour défendre et plus de lucidité devant le but. On a eu la possession mais quand tu ne cadres pas un tir..Notre production est insuffisante et la situation devient préoccupante »

#2437. Sports club members becoming less tolerant of homosexuality

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Acceptance of homosexuality in Dutch sports clubs has declined significantly in the last generation, according to a survey of attitudes by the Mulier Institute.

The organisation found that 66% of people had no objection to a fellow member of a sports club being gay, while in 2008 the figure was 85%.

Just over half (55%) of respondents said they had no problem sharing a shower with a gay team-mate of the same sex, which also represented a drop from 73% in 2008.

The Mulier Institute said the findings reflected a social trend that has also been seen in schools, where the proportion of boys aged between 12 and 16 with a positive view of homosexuality has dropped from 40% to 22% since 2021.

The Dutch Olympic Committee NOC*NSF said the findings were “highly regrettable” and pledged to step up its efforts to make sport more inclusive.

But the John Blankenstein Foundation, which campaigns for LGBT emancipation in sport, said it had noticed declining enthusiasm for its workshops and growing numbers of parents who voiced objections.

Karin Blankenstein, who set up the organisation in 2008, told NOS: “I get the sensitivity around transgender people in sport at the top level, but this is about amateur sport.”

#2436. Christian Lopez : "J'ai vu des jeunes Verts entreprenants, déterminés, solidaires"

Christian Lopez revient pour nous sur le succès des réservistes stéphanois sur le terrain qui porte son nom.

Christian, tu as donné hier le coup d’envoi fictif du match que la réserve a remporté sur un terrain qui porte ton nom au Cannet-Rocheville, tout près de chez toi !

Effectivement, j’habite à 100 mètres du stade ! Depuis quelques années le terrain d’honneur porte mon nom et le terrain annexe porte le nom de Bruno Bellone, qui est issu lui aussi du Cannet-Rocheville. Bruno jouait ici avant d’intégrer le centre de formation de l’AS Monaco. C’est au Cannet-Rocheville que j'ai commencé à jouer au football à 10 ou 11 ans. A l’époque il y avait deux clubs, l'AS Rocheville et le Sporting Club du Cannet. Moi je jouais à l'AS Rocheville. Les deux clubs ont fusionné en mai 1968 pour devenir l'Entente Sportive du Cannet-Rocheville et j'en suis parti pour venir à Saint-Etienne, j'avais 16 ans.

Cela fait 27 ans que je suis revenu m’installer au Cannet. Pendant les 4 premières années, j'ai été au centre de formation de l'AS Cannes. J'ai été entraîneur là-bas, puis après entraîneur et directeur du centre. Quand l’AS Cannes a perdu le statut professionnel et donc le centre de formation, il ne pouvait pas me garder. A ce moment-là, comme j'avais sympathisé avec Madame la députée Michèle Tabarot et son frère Philippe (actuellement Ministre des Transports), je leur avais proposé d’intégrer le club et d’être intégré au service des sports de la mairie.

C’est ce qui s’est passé. J’exerce actuellement mon 2e mandat en tant qu’adjoint au maire du Cannet en tant que délégué aux Sports et à la Jeunesse. J’ai effectivement entraîné le club de la commune et j’en ai assuré la direction sportive. Je suis toujours membre du comité directeur de l’ES Cannet-Rocheville. J’ai été dans l’opérationnel mais j’ai maintenant 73 ans, à la retraite. Je suis bien sûr l’équipe première et assiste notamment à tous les matches à domicile. On me pose des questions sur le sportif, je donne mon avis.

Qu’as-tu pensé du match d’hier soir qui a opposé tes deux clubs de cœur ?

Déjà, bravo aux jeunes Verts qui ont su arracher la victoire ! Ce qui n'est pas bon pour nous, parce qu’on reste encore dans le bas du classement. J’ai vu une équipe stéphanoise où il y a de la qualité. Une équipe joueuse, qui ne se relâche pas. Ces jeunes Verts ne lâchent rien, j’aime cette mentalité ! Elle leur a permis de revenir au score et de prendre l'avantage dans les arrêts de jeu.

Le résultat reflète la physionomie du match ?

Je dirais que l’ASSE a su aller chercher ce succès. Un match nul n’aurait pas été illogique. On a eu le mérite d’ouvrir le score en seconde période mais ensuite on a été un peu naïfs, on a continué à attaquer comme si on avait un score à remonter alors qu'on menait. Il y a eu quelques oublis, des fautes de marquage et on l’a payé cash car il y a de la qualité en face. Je trouve qu’on a manqué de rigueur défensive. Même à 1-1, on a continué à attaquer alors qu'on était souvent pris sur des contre-attaques stéphanoises.

J'étais un peu énervé à la fin du match parce qu’on l’a perdu en encaissant deux buts dans les ultimes minutes. On n'a pas le droit parce qu'on a 3 ou 4 joueurs d'expérience dans notre équipe. On n'a pas le droit de partir à l'abordage quand on arrive vers la fin et qu'on sait que depuis le début de la saison, on perd des matchs dans les dernières minutes. À un moment donné, il devrait y avoir des joueurs qui prennent en main la direction de l'équipe. Il y a des postes clés dans une équipe. On est parti à l'abordage et on s’est fait prendre en contre.

Quels joueurs stéphanois t’ont tapé dans l’œil ?

Le numéro 5, Nathan Kasia, je l’ai trouvé très bon. C’est un jeune défenseur central de 17 ans qui me semble prometteur. Il a de la présence dans les duels, une bonne lecture du jeu et des qualités dans la relance. Le numéro 11 Etienne Mendy est un ailier gauche très percutant, très rapide, il a mis à rude épreuve notre défense. Comme il s’est beaucoup dépensé, il a été remplacé par le numéro 14, Noah Moulin, qui a fait une bonne entrée. C’est lui qui a centré sur le but victorieux d’un autre entrant, le numéro 15 Lamine Sonko.

Ce joueur nous aura fait très mal car c’est déjà lui qui avait égalisé quelques minutes auparavant. Il a mis deux vrais buts d’attaquant.  Au-delà des performances individuelles, j’ai apprécié les valeurs affichées par ce collectif stéphanois. J’ai vu des jeunes entreprenants, déterminés, solidaires. Il faut dire que ce sont des gamins qui s'entraînent tous les jours. Ils sont dans un centre de formation pour devenir des footballeurs professionnels. Nous on est dans le monde du foot amateur. Nos joueurs ne s'entraînent que trois fois dans la semaine.

A l’issue du match d’hier soir, l’entraîneur stéphanois Sylvain Gibert nous a confié qu’il avait été d’autant plus honoré de te rencontrer qu’il t’avait cité en exemple dans des causeries la saison dernière. Que tu représentais bien l’âme du club, cette capacité à ne jamais renoncer...

Cela me touche. Je l'ai vu avant la rencontre avec son staff dont Romain Hamouma et on a eu l'occasion d'échanger après le match. J'ai beaucoup aprécié ce moment. C'est toujours super d’être pris en exemple. Mais c’est aussi pour ça, ayant gardé l’âme d’un compétiteur, que ça m’agace vraiment qu’on ait perdu ce match comme on l’a perdu, alors qu’on menait encore à la 86e minute… Si j’avais joué, je ne les aurais pas pris ces buts ! On savait qu’il y avait des jeunes joueurs talentueux dans cette équipe stéphanoise, des garçons capables au dernier moment de te marquer un ou deux buts. Mais alors qu’on avait le match en main, on n’a pas réussi à les contenir !

Grâce à cette victoire arraché sur tes terres, la réserve stéphanoise s’est hissée à la 2e place. Quelques heures plus tard, l’équipe première a quant à elle consolidé son statut de leader de la Ligue 2 en dominant de faibles Lavallois.

Je n’ai pas vu le match mais je me réjouis que les Verts aient renoué avec le succès après leur faux pas à Guingamp. Cette victoire accrédite la thèse de Ian Cathro selon laquelle la lourde défaite au Roudourou n’était qu’un accident de parcours. Je suis plutôt optimiste quant à l’issue de cette saison. Sur ce que j’ai vu cette saison, l’équipe me paraît meilleure que celle de la saison passée. Je la trouve plus solide, plus solidaire. Les joueurs qui sont là jouent sérieusement. La saison dernière, sur le peu de matchs que j'ai vus, chaque fois qu’on perdait un ballon, je tremblais. Cette saison l’équipe dégage plus de sérénité, affiche davantage de maîtrise. J’espère évidemment que l’ASSE va poursuivre sur sa lancée et regagner sa place dans l’élite dans quelques mois.

#2434. Bayern chief unfazed by Upamecano release clause reports

After lengthy negotiations, Bayern Munich announced a contract extension until 2030 for Dayot Upamecano in February. However, according to reports, the agreement came at a price, with a €65 million release clause included.

Given the current state of the transfer market, such a fee would arguably represent a bargain for a player of Upamecano’s calibre.

However, while neither confirming nor denying the reports, Bayern board member for sport Max Eberl didn't appear particularly concerned when asked about the release clause at the weekend.

“I’m not here to explain the details of contracts," Eberl was quoted as saying by Absolut Bayern.

“One thing is clear: we have extended Upamecano’s contract, we’re absolutely delighted that we have, and, honestly, he feels incredibly comfortable here.”

Bayern themselves activated a €42.5 million release clause to sign the French centre-back from RB Leipzig in 2021.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

A late equaliser for Fortuna Sittard in De Kuip proved costly for Feyenoord as PSV and Twente racked up huge victories to move within two points of the Eredivisie leaders.

Feyenoord paid the price for failing to finish off the Limburgers, with Luciano Valente’s 59th-minute goal the only reward for their dominance.

Fortuna equalised with four minutes left when Shiloh ’t Zand, on loan from Feyenoord, was allowed to run through to the penalty area and beat Tjark Ernst with a low shot.

Feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst made no effort to hide his disappointment. “We know that Fortuna are the kind of team who can score from the few attacks they have,” he said. “If you don’t score the goals, things like this can happen.”

Second-placed Ajax are a point behind after a narrow win at home against AZ ended an 11-match winless streak against the Alkmaar club, as Tolu Arokodare’s early header proved decisive.

Twente recorded the biggest win of the weekend with a 9-0 demolition of Excelsior in Rotterdam, with Wout Weghorst scoring four times and Sondre Ørjasaeter notching up five assists.

Excelsior collapsed following the fifth-minute dismissal of Nesto Groen for a reckless high challenge. The home side were 5-0 down at half-time, with Weghorst claiming a hat-trick in the opening 33 minutes.

PSV bagged seven goals in a one-sided encounter with bottom club Willem II, with all the goals coming from different scorers including Ricardo Pepi, who came on in the second half after a six-week absence through injury.

Telstar opened up a three-point gap at the bottom over ADO Den Haag with a 4-2 win against Utrecht in a painful return to Velsen-Zuid for Telstar’s former coach Anthony Correia.

ADO went down 1-0 in Zwolle, with PEC’s Dylan Mbayo scoring the only goal with a first-time finish on the stroke of half-time.

The match between Cambuur Leeuwarden and Go Ahead Eagles was suspended in the 82nd minute after visiting fans threw fireworks onto the pitch.

The clubs agreed with the KNVB not to play the final minutes and allow Cambuur’s 4-0 advantage to stand as the final result.

Go Ahead’s director Jan-Willem van Dop said the club would take action against those responsible: “I am ashamed on behalf a small group of supporters who ruined things for the club and a large hare of the fans in the away end,” he said.

#2429. Les Amazones reçues 5 sur 5

Désormais seules en tête de l'Arkema Seconde Ligue, les Amazones se déplaçaient ce dimanche à Lille où elles se sont imposées 1-0 grâce à une Ithaisa Vinoly impériale dans les buts et un but tardif d'Héloïse Mansuy. Un cinquième succès consécutif en championnat qui permet à l'ASSE de conforter sa place de leader et de semer la concurrence !Après leur victoire convaincante face à Auxerre (2-0), les Vertes faisaient face dans le Nord à un concurrent sérieux dans la course à la montée et Yannick Chandioux devait en plus composer sans Rachel Corboz et Agathe Felden, absentes surprises de dernière minute.Sur la pelouse synthétique du LOSC, ce qui avait obligé les Stéphanoises à s'entraîner toute la semaine sur une surface identique à Saint-Priest-en-Jarez, les Vertes ne connaissaient pourtant pas l'entame espérée, les Lilloises imposant rapidement leur rythme et se montrant particulièrement agressives dans les duels. Dès la 9e minute, la meilleure buteuse de D2, Coralie Monguillon se présentait face à Ithaisa Vinoly, mais la gardienne espagnole remportait son face-à-face et préservait les cages stéphanoises.Le LOSC continuait de pousser et Wissem Bouzid voyait ensuite une nouvelle tentative dangereuse contrée in extremis avant que Chloé Neller ne trouve le poteau à quelques minutes de la pause. Côté stéphanois, seule Sarah Cambot parvenait à répondre sur une belle reprise de volée qui frôlait le montant adverse. A la pause, les Vertes pouvaient s'estimer heureuses de ne pas être menées.Mais au retour des vestiaires, les Amazones affichaient de meilleures intentions et se montraient davantage entreprenantes, même si les Lilloises continuaient de poser de sérieux problèmes à l'arrière-garde verte. À l'heure de jeu, un énorme cafouillage dans la surface stéphanoise faisait même passer un sérieux frisson dans le camp forézien avant de finir en corner.Les minutes défilaient et les joueuses de Yannick Chandioux peinaient toujours à prendre véritablement le contrôle de la rencontre. À la 74e minute, Coralie Monguillon se heurtait encore à une Ithaisa Vinoly exceptionnelle. La portière espagnole réalisait une parade déterminante et permettait aux siennes de rester dans le match.Et ce ne fut pas en vain car à 10 minutes de la fin du match, sur un coup de pied arrêté, un ballon traînait dans les cinq mètres cinquante nordistes et Héloïse Mansuy surgissait pour le pousser au fond des filets. Un avantage aussi précieux qu'inattendu (0-1, 80e) !Les dernières minutes devenaient alors particulièrement tendues, les Lilloises vexées tentant de revenir au score par tous les moyens possibles, faisant progressivement monter la nervosité entre les deux bancs.Sans surprise, la tension dégénéra et entraîna une pluie de cartons à la 90e minute, l'entraîneur lillois Mathieu Robail et la buteuse Coralie Monguillon étant ainsi expulsés mais malgré cette fin de rencontre particulièrement agitée, les Vertes ne lâchaient rien et conservaient leur avantage jusqu'au coup de sifflet final.Un précieux succès, acquis dans la douleur, qui permettait aux Amazones d'enchaîner une cinquième victoire consécutive en championnat et de prolonger leur invincibilité.Yannick Chandioux: "On retiendra avant tout la victoire. Et celle-ci, on la doit en grande partie à notre gardienne, Ithaïsa. Elle nous a maintenues dans le match pendant longtemps, alors que nous sommes passées à côté de notre entame, quasiment dès les premières minutes. Nous avons été moins agressives que les Lilloises, qui ont pleinement joué sur cet aspect et nous ont mises en difficulté (...) Ne pas avoir encaissé de but dans cette rencontre relève presque du petit hold-up. (...) Parfois, les saisons réussies se construisent aussi dans ce genre de matchs, que l'on parvient à gagner alors que peu de monde nous voyait l'emporter".Avec 17 points au compteur, les Stéphanoises conservent bien sûr leur fauteuil de leader avec deux longueurs d'avance sur Le Mans et trois sur Roubaix. Elles retrouveront leur public samedi prochain au stade Salif-Keita face à Nice, l'actuel 10e... d'un championnat à 11

#2427. Dual passports issue continues to plague Dutch-based footballers

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Dutch-born footballers who were called up to play for former colonies such as Suriname and Indonesia are still in limbo over their national status, six months after the “passportgate” crisis first flared up.

Suriname’s parliament passed a law in September enabling players who are selected for the national team to gain citizenship automatically.

But the Dutch immigration service IND said the law passed in Suriname made no difference to the rules on dual nationality in the Netherlands.

“The fact that Surinamese nationality has been obtained by legal means is not enough on its own to qualify for one of the exceptional categories under our law,” a spokesman for the Dutch justice ministry told broadcaster NOS.

The law was intended to settle the question of dual nationality for footballers, which arose last March when NAC Breda challenged the eligibility of Go Ahead Eagles defender Dean James.

James took Indonesian citizenship last year after accepting an invitation to play for the national team, but under Dutch dual nationality rules he was required to give up his original passport.

The Dutch football association KNVB launched an investigation into the employment status of players who were called up by countries such as Suriname, Cape Verde and Indonesia. In the meantime it arranged for Dutch-based players to be given temporary work permits so they could keep playing for their clubs.

Losing Dutch nationality also stripped them of their EU citizenship, meaning they would need to obtain visas and meet stricter criteria, such as an annual salary threshold of €600,000, to be eligible to play in the Eredivisie.

Several players have passed up invitations to join the Surinamese squad because of the uncertainty, including Danilho Doekhi of Lazio, Milan van Ewijk of Coventry City and Jayden Oosterwolde of Fenerbahçe.

National team manager Henk Fraser said it was “inexplicable” that players’ livelihoods were being damaged by their desire to play international football.

“Both countries have to get together and clarify the situation,” he told NOS. “This is a straightforward case of people following their hearts and wanting to play for Suriname, but not knowing where they stand.”

Some players said they felt misled by the Surinamese football association, which told them they were playing for the national team on “sports passports” that allowed them to remain Dutch citizens.

Former Feyenoord winger Jean-Paul Boëtius said he only discovered after he was first called up for Suriname last year that he had inadvertently renounced his Dutch citizenship as a result.

Shortly afterwards he received a letter from the city council in Rotterdam telling him to hand in his Dutch passport, which he had recently renewed, because it was no longer valid.

“I now have a sticker in my Surinamese passport that says I have a residency permit allowing me to live in the Netherlands,” he told NOS. “But that’s only for a year. It’s a very difficult situation. I want to become Dutch again. I was born and brought up here.”

#2422. "Call it a day, Manu!" – Bayern legend urges Neuer to call time on his career

Germany goalkeeping icon Sepp Maier believes it's time for Manuel Neuer to hang up his gloves at the end of the season.

Asked by Sport1 what he would tell Neuer if the Bayern goalkeeper called him to ask whether he should continue playing beyond the summer of 2027, Maier responded:

“I would tell him, ‘Call it a day, Manu!’ You have given football an incredible amount, you have won everything and you no longer have anything to prove to anyone.

“Manuel has had an incredible career and revolutionised goalkeeping. But at some point, the body no longer holds up the way you would like it to. And even Manuel Neuer can't stop that moment from coming,” Maier also said in the interview, while stressing that the 40-year-old has to make the decision for himself.

Having already missed several games this season, Neuer suffered another setback in Saturday's 2-1 win over Mainz, with a tendon tear expected to keep him out for several weeks.

With Neuer having spent so much time on the sidelines, 23-year-old Jonas Urbig – widely regarded as his successor at Bayern – has already made eight appearances this season.

Following Neuer's latest injury setback, some have suggested that Bayern should make Urbig their first-choice goalkeeper already, and Maier also weighed in on the debate:

“At some point, you have to take that step. Manuel is 40 years old and Jonas Urbig is the future of Bayern Munich. But you cannot simply write Manuel off either. If he is fit and performing well, he should be allowed to play. However, Bayern need to make a clear decision sooner rather than later. This constant back-and-forth does neither goalkeeper any favours,” he said.

“When Manuel is fully fit, I still consider him one of the best goalkeepers. His experience, presence and understanding of the game are truly exceptional. But the crucial question is: how often is he still fully fit? Being world-class is no use if your body can no longer keep up. And Jonas Urbig is doing a good job. You shouldn't underestimate him either.”

#2420. Top five football betting tips and tricks

Football is the world’s most famous sport, and it is the sport of choice of a great many sports punters as well. Especially popular in Europe, betting on football can be an incredibly profitable enterprise, so long as you know how to do it.

Getting started on football betting is far from easy, though. This form of gambling requires dedication, investment, and persistence. As you gain experience, your intuition will improve and you will be able to make more correct predictions.

But experience is not the only thing that can help you become a better football punter. In fact, you can substantially improve your betting strategy by simply following some basic football betting tips.

You might find shopping around boring and unhelpful, but you just have to do it when you search sites for football betting. As you know, the higher the odds, the bigger the payout. What you may have missed, however, is that odds are different at each bookmaker. Having said that, shopping around for the best odds is sensible, as it rewards you with bigger payouts.

In this line of thought, sticking to one bookmaker is virtually pointless. Even if the bookie of your choosing offers the best odds for a number of matches, it is highly unlikely that their odds will remain the best for long.

An obvious one, we know. And yet, you will be surprised by the number of football bettors who wager on football, but do not follow the sport. So, why is it important to follow the action closely?

First of all, by watching football matches, you can take part in the most exciting football betting market – the live betting market. What is more important, however, is that following the action provides an invaluable insight into teams and players’ style, condition, and determination – important factors  to consider when placing a bet.

As you watch more and more games, you will improve your analytic abilities. In time, you will be able to make more accurate predictions about the outcome of different matches, which, of course,  will result in placing more winning bets.

As you know, odds are based on the probability of occurrence of a certain outcome; the higher the odds, the more unlikely it is for that outcome to actually occur. But what happens when the odds offered by the bookmaker represent a probability that is lower than the actual probability of an outcome occurring? In such a situation, you can place what is called a value bet.

If you want to become a professional football punter, you should always search for value when betting, as it leads to huge profits

Favoured by beginners in particular, accumulators are a type of football wager which allows you to bet on as many fixtures as you like. Most commonly, you will be asked to choose a match winner, but as the market is diverse, you may be offered a number of other betting options. What makes accumulators an appealing betting market is the huge potential payout – here, you can stake as little as £1 and have the potential to win more than £500,000, depending on the bookmaker and the number of selected fixtures.

If you find accumulators’ payouts too good to be true, you are right. As a matter of fact, there is a reason for the odds to be set so high – actually winning an accumulator bet, especially one which involves a wide selection of matches, is nearly impossible. You see, all you need for your whole wager to lose is one wrong prediction. For example, if you bet on 10 matches and just one of them goes wrong, your entire accumulator is lost.

To make money by betting on football, avoid betting on accumulators – the risk is simply not worth it.

Finally, if you want to be a successful football punter, learn how not to mix emotions with betting. This is easier said than done, though.

Whenever your favourite team plays, you want them to win, regardless of how (im)possible that may be. If you do not learn how to leave emotions out of betting, however, you are highly likely to put money on your favourite team even if they have no chance of winning the match. Conversely, should you base your bets on hard facts and not on emotions, you increase your chances to win.

Our advice – avoid betting on fixtures that involve one of your favourite teams, that is the easiest way to keep emotions at bay.

#2419. Feyenoord facing fireworks fine after 3-0 loss to Internazionale

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Feyenoord are facing a heavy fine from European football authorities after fireworks were let off during their Champions League defeat by Internazionale.

Referee Glenn Nyberg suspended the match for several minutes after flares were fired onto the roof from outside De Kuip stadium, damaging the structure. Police later made two arrests.

“It’s obviously not right and it’ll be another fine,” coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst said wearily after the game, which ended in a comprehensive 3-0 defeat for his team.

One flare landed on the pitch despite the club taking measures such as hanging nets from the gantries to stop objects being thrown from the stands. “They’re letting off fireworks from outside now,” Van Bronckhorst said. “What do you do about that?”

Uefa are likely to hit Feyenoord with a fine and could order the club to close parts of the stadium for their next home matches in the competition, against Porto on November 24 and RB Leipzig on January 27.

The club also have a suspended penalty hanging over them from last October, when they were fined €60,000 after fans let off fireworks during the match against Greek club Panathinaikos.

On the pitch, Feyenoord were undone by a classic display of Italian defending and counter-attacking, as Internazionale sat back after taking an eighth-minute lead through Yann Bisseck.

Francesco Pio Esposito headed in a second early in the second half, just as Feyenoord were pushing for an equaliser, before Piotr Zielinski made sure of the win with a shot from 20 metres.

Captain Luciano Valente said the result was “more than deserved” and the visitors had shown more “quality”.

“This defeat was harder to take than the one against Barcelona,” he told Ziggo Sport. “Because we thought going in that we could get something, but we just weren’t good enough.”

Van Bronckhorst said he was not surprised by the difference in class between the teams. “They scored the first goal out of nothing,” he said. “And Inter know better what the game needs at every stage.

“Their players have a lot of experience, they’ve been in the final twice in the last four years. So we’re at a disadvantage.”

Non deve pensare alla pressione, deve metterci entusiasmo. Ci deve aiutare, sta bene fisicamente, l'abbiamo perso per 4-5 giorni, ma sta migliorando tantissimo.

#2414. PSV edged out by sharper Club Brugge in Champions League defeat

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

PSV Eindhoven endured a frustrating night in the Champions League as their defensive frailties were exposed in a 2-1 defeat by Club Brugge.

PSV started full of attacking intent and should have taken an early lead when Ivan Perisic put Sergiño Dest clean through on goal, but the defender’s shot was too close to goalkeeper Yann Sommer.

Instead it was the visitors who took the lead with their first real attack when Nicolo Tresoldi headed in a teasing cross from Joaquin Seys.

PSV equalised early in the second half as an outstanding pass by Sven Mijnans into the path Lutsharel Geertruida allowed the defender to charge to the byline. His pullback found its way to Kodai Sano, whose shot took a deflection off Seys into the net.

But five minutes later PSV were caught out as another razor-sharp pass by Seys released Carlos Forbs in space to net the winner.

The home side refused to give up, but were unable to find a way past Sommer in the closing stages as the Belgian side closed out the win.

Team captain Mauro Junior admitted that PSV had been undone by shortcomings at the back. “We had a lot of opportunities in the first half but we didn’t score,” he told Ziggo Sport.

“We want to attack and score goals, but we weren’ well organised today in defence. We need to keep our heads up and look forward to the next game.”

The result leaves PSV in 24th place, just above the elimination line, ahead of their next match away to Real Madrid on November 24, with four points from their opening four matches.

#2410. Opinion: The morality of football

Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.

Is football a moral force for good? That was the question of the day, and each of the four guests were asked to discuss various aspects of the debate from financial fairplay to club takeovers by foreign entities to racism.

Nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly. Is there a greater significance to the game we are watching, or is it merely 22 humans kicking a leather ball into a net?

Join Nathan as he elaborates on the most significant takeaways of what was a fascinating discussion on the sport and morality in general.

Football, for some, may be the most poignant reminder of the moral universe in which we live. While debate has raged for centuries regarding the precise origin of moral absolutes and how humans ought to live, it is simply unavoidable to say humanity is often troubled by events surrounding the game we all love so dearly.

In not so distant history, every normal act of human life would have been assigned some degree of moral significance. Every action had inherently moral indicators - for good or for evil. Today, postmodern views of morality dominate. These describe morality as an entirely subjective dimension. In other words, it cannot be pinned down exactly whether behaviors are objectively good or bad. We can only find fault with someone else’s interpretation based on their own unique moral code. Morality is relative to the individual or society.

Yet last night’s dialogue concerning football and human behavior was filled with moral accusations and claims which strongly suggested humans are not content with relativist morality. Indeed, we are at times frightened by and disgusted with what we observe in and around football. Our sense of moral justice is deeply disturbed. But with respect to what exactly?

In responding to the panelist’s questions, I observed a familiar paradigm. Each time I have discussed any aspect of moral behavior, the speculation humans are good or at worst morally neutral animals continually reemerges. This widely accepted presupposition is then followed shortly by disgust at some aspect of human behavior. Almost as if to ask “why are all these good humans behaving so badly?” while ignoring the very real implications of this line of inquiry. A question rendered unanswerable by the insistent a priori assumptions from which it was derived.

If humans are intrinsically beneficent, conscientious, fair, humble, and honest then why is football rife with racism, misogyny, greed, disenfranchisement, lies, cheating, violence, and the hypocrisy to deny the occurrence of any such behaviors except when a rival club is the guilty party? Behaviors which are perpetrated by individual supporters, fanatical groups, club administrations, corporate bodies such as FIFA, political entities, nations, and even the players themselves. No one participating faction is guiltless.

To so blithely sidestep more sufficient explanations for the empirical reality of wickedness in football and in human behavior more generally is not just factually incorrect. It undermines real attempts to understand the root of these behaviors where they might be dealt with more effectively.

To listen to The Moral Maze episode entitled “Football: a moral force for good?” produced by BBC radio and featuring PortuGOAL’s Seleção correspondent Nathan Motz click on this link

Furthermore, in good faith, how successful is a response against heinous evil when those perpetrating it are regarded as behaving in accord with their unique moral ambitions? Humans refuse to accept their indisputably objective moral lacking at a fundamental level. This restricts us from ever doing any more than “stamping out” the alleged impropriety of others – while we ourselves may readily engage in these very same behaviors. Moral relativism cannot account for the moral outrage emanating from all corners of the football world. Is Qatar wrong to perpetrate human rights atrocities or is it allowable because their culture is indifferent? Is hooliganism objectively wrong, or only when someone else’s club is responsible?

The overlooking of our own failings while lashing out at others for theirs is quintessential to the morally fallen nature of humanity itself. Football tells all. There are not good people and bad people. There are only people who both willfully and unintentionally transgress the moral code embedded in each of our hearts. A moral law which can only have ever been given by a moral Lawgiver. Otherwise, it is truly your word against mine as it pertains to the moral validity of all behaviors - even those which may deeply violate your conscience.

Football generates an episodic, semantic, and imagistic description of universal archetypes: good and evil, sacrifice and greed, cruelty and mercy, hero and anti-hero. It speaks to every arc of life’s plotline: tragedy, comedy, victory, defeat, the finite nature of our circumstances. It is one of the preeminent existential dialects alongside religion, visual art, written and spoken language, music, and theatre. Football plucks a primal chord.

As metaphysics have been curtailed to just physics in the modern secular West, football has only elevated our awareness of the often dire moral predicaments of our species. Yet it is clear the moral conversation does not originate on a football pitch. The pitch is but a grand stage upon which moral themes may be observed and critiqued, a mirror held in front of our own soul.

The desire for ultimate purpose, for meaning beyond the material realm, never disappeared in modernity. Arguably, it has only become more desperate as the outcry for ultimate significance comes under more scrutiny and criticism by those who constrain ontological explanations to those accounted for by physics. The severity of the mental health crisis in the West is in no small part explained by the terrifying existential awareness we are cut adrift in an abstract sea of meaningless, hopeless wandering between two oblivions - that before mortal life began and that at mortal life’s end. Let football be one voice which reassures you - there is ultimate meaning and good reasons why football so unsettles our craving for justice.

In a palpable, unavoidable way, football and supporter communities across Europe are encountering moral quandaries. In Portugal, age-old debates between FC Porto and Benfica have routinely been haunted by, in many cases, farcical and cynical hypocrisy. Throughout its history, the FPF has been susceptible to showing partiality to a club, player, or style which ultimately degrades the performance of our beloved Seleção. Deny it all we like, and not one aspect of this reality is changed.

In conclusion, whatever your thoughts or beliefs on the subject of moral significance, its origin, the meaning of life, and how football draws that out, I hope it will be beneficial to examine these matters more deeply. In my zeal, I admit I have not always been prudent to initiate these discussions in a way which respects thoughtful disagreement. It is my hope this effort to bring that discussion to Portuguese football will be well-received and carefully pondered. But I will contentedly listen to those followers who may be genuinely unhappy or unsupportive of this or any other idea about which I write.

The readers of this website and the larger Portuguese football loving world are my people. It is a joy and a responsibility I take seriously whenever I have the opportunity to raise important questions about the Selecao, the game, and our lives in general.

#2408. U15 : de la joie contre les Caladois

Les U15 de Benjamin Petit pouvaient être heureux à la fin de leur match contre les Caladois du FC Villefranche Beaujolais. A l'issue d'une rencontre très disputée, comme souvent dans cet exigeant championnat, ils n'ont rien lâché face à un adversaire de valeur et ont su trouver les ressources pour l'emporter. Cela récompense leur volonté d'aller de l'avant, leur ténacité et leur concentration dans l'aspect défensif. Sans quelques joueurs retenus avec les U16 de Kevin De Jesus (Ilan Clapeyron, Riad Moutae, Kaïs Boukerma et Hugo Durin) tous ont su se mettre au diapason, et cette victoire est celle d'un collectif très solidaire.

L'entame du match a été stéphanoise, les Verts s'installant dans le camp caladois. Dès la 9ème minute, sur un centre venu de la gauche, Nolan Lebreton remettait pour Charly Davignon qui était devancé de peu par un défenseur. Deux minutes plus tard, un coup-franc de ce même Nolan Lebreton était capté par le gardien. Les Verts monopolisaient le ballon mais le dernier geste, souvent dans les petits espaces, manquait de justesse pour mettre de conclure. Peu à peu, Villefranche déserrait l'étreinte stéphanoise et se montrait dangereux sur coup de pied arrêté, mais Manoa Frison faisait bonne garde, notamment, à la 26ème, où il réalisait une double parade avant que Victor Hamouma ne s'interpose pour stopper la tentative adverse. Quelques minutes plus tard, Charly Davignon, qui repiquait au centre, était victime d'une faute laquelle donnait lieu à un coup-franc. Nolhan Fernandes le frappait et mettait le gardien à contribution. Peu après sur un long centre de Nolhan Fernandes, Hugo Bastide obtenait un corner. Ce corner, joué à deux, permettait à Nolan Lebreton d'adresser un long centre au deuxième poteau que le portier caladois dégageait. Les contres de Villefranche butaient sur une solide défense stéphanoise, concentrée et rigoureuse qui gérait bien les espaces et s'attachait à ressortir proprement les ballons. Le score était donc nul et vierge au repos.

La deuxième mi-temps repartait sur les mêmes bases, avec une maitrîse verte retrouvée et des situations intéressantes, sans parvenir toutefois à faire la différence.  Mais les Verts, suite à un carton blanc à la 54ème minute, se retrouvaient réduits à 10 pendant une dizaine de minutes, et ce fait de jeu freinait un peu leur dynamique. Ils allaient trouver la faille suite à un cafouillage dans la surface, avec une main adverse et un accrochage sur Mathis La Rosa. Toujours est-il que l'arbitre sanctionnait cette action d'un penalty que Charly Davignon transformait, donnant l'avantage aux Verts (68ème). La fin du match allait être plutôt hâchée avec plusieurs coups-de-pied arrêtés que Villefranche jouait directement. Les Verts se créaient cependant quelques opportunités mais un manque de justesse ne leur permettait pas de les concrétiser. Le match se terminait donc sur cette victoire stéphanoise somme toute logique, tant elle avait été bien construite.

La composition : Frison - Bergougnoux (Uneau, 50ème), L. La Rosa, Hamouma, Bastide - Wojcik (Davignon, 50ème), M.La Rosa, Lebreton - Fernandes (Madjidi, 50ème), Maganga Verrier, Davignon (Linganzi, 41ème).

La réaction de Benjamin Petit : "Le match a été serré, très disputé face à une bonne équipe de Villefranche, comme souvent dans ce championnat. Il n'y a pas de match facile et c'est un bon apprentissage pour les jeunes. Nous avons fait vingt premières minutes plutôt intéressantes, avec de la maîtrise, une volonté de défendre en avançant, un point que travaillons. Nous avons baissé en fin de première mi-temps, avec plus de difficulté à maintenir notre pression, ce qui nous a menés à défendre plus bas. En conclusion, je dirais que globalement, nous avons eu la maîtrise, mais mon regret est le manque de justesse, de percussion et d'efficacité pour créer du danger sur le but adverse et se mettre à l'abri. Je retiens notre solidité défensive, notre rigueur dans les prises en charge, notre détermination à ne rien encaisser, notamment sur les coups-de-pied arrêtés, un domaine dans lequel nous avons progressé. Il faudra néanmoins éviter certaines fautes, évitables, qui offrent des situations dangereuses à l'adversaire. C'était un match intéressant dans l'apprentissage, la gestion des temps forts et des temps faibles. Il faut toutefois  essayer d'être plus efficace dans nos temps forts tout en restant solides dans les temps faibles."

Fa decisamente la differenza sulle fasce e firma anche il quarto assist stagionale. Come il resto della squadra finisce per spegnersi nella ripresa.

La Lazio domina il primo tempo e rischia di chiudere con più di un gol di scarto. Nella ripresa, complici gli infortuni di Sutalo e Tavares, il calo è evidente, ma portare un punto a casa su un campo così difficile non è mai scontato.

#2405. Klopp set to hold talks with Nmecha over controversial religious celebration

Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is expected to hold talks with Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha after the midfielder's controversial crown celebration sparked debate over the weekend, according to Bild.

When Nmecha bagged a brace in Borussia Dortmund's 2-1 win over SV Elversberg on Saturday, he celebrated by kneeling down, removing an imaginary crown and placing it on the ground.

The celebration is associated with the evangelical network “Ballers in God”, which LGBTQ+ organisations have classified as “Christian fundamentalist”, and its campaign “The King's Return”.

According to research by, among others, ARD's Monitor programme, parts of the religious group hold homophobic and anti-LGBTQ+ views and describe abortion as “Satan's plan”.

The celebration prompted Borussia Dortmund's Supporters Council to criticise the midfielder over the weekend and call on the club to clearly distance itself from evangelical networks.

Now, with Nmecha joining the German national team for the upcoming international fixtures as part of Jürgen Klopp's 24-man squad, a conversation with the coach about the celebration is reportedly on the cards.

German Football Association sporting director Rudi Völler addressed the issue on the podcast Kerners 11.

“Of course, there is freedom of religion and freedom of belief. Everyone is free to express their faith in their own way. Some people like it, others don't. Naturally, we will speak to him about it again, because it has now become a public issue. The most important thing with an issue like this is that you first have to understand it properly. We have to ensure that the processes surrounding these matters are handled correctly," Völler said, via Bild.

“So far, I can only say positive things about Felix. He did an outstanding job at the World Cup – not just as a footballer, but also in the way he behaved between matches. He is extremely popular with his teammates and is a thoroughly decent person.

“But I can understand the debate and that not everyone likes it. As I said, we will handle it in a similar way to Dortmund – we are in contact with them. But we shouldn't blow it out of proportion either. We will certainly speak to him about it.”

Nmecha also performed the celebration after scoring in Germany's 7-1 win over Curaçao at last summer's World Cup.

Al Maradona Napoli-Lazio finisce 1-1. #2402. Les U16 n'ont pas fait de détail

Après leur déconvenue d'il y a trois semaines, et la défaite face au CASCOL Oullins à l'extrême limite du temps additionnel (3-2), les U16 de Kevin De Jesus avaient à coeur de réagir. La trêve avait été meublée par une rencontre amicale à Bourg-Peronnas remportée par 3 à 0 (buts de N.Fontaine et Joris Rochette 2), histoire de garder le rythme et de parfaire les automatismes. Les Verts se présentaient hier, sur le terrain synthétique Georges Bereta, avec une équipe dans laquelle figuraient quatre U15 (Ilan Clapeyron, Riad Moutae, Kaïs Boukerma et Hugo Durin) face à la lanterne rouge, l'AFCA (Aurillac Foot Cantal Auvergne) qui, il faut bien l'avouer, n'a pas opposé une farouche résistance aux Verts. Ces derniers l'ont en effet emporté sur le large score de 9 à 0, alors qi'ils menaient déjà 4-0 au repos.

Ce match a ressemblé à une attaque-défense, digne d'un match de handball. Dès la 2ème minute, Hugo Durin se mettait déjà en évidence avec un tir au ras du poteau. Dans la foulée, à la réception d'un ballon venu de la droite, il éliminait son adversaire et marquait  d'un tir au ras du sol. (ASSE-AFCA : 1-0, 3ème).Le jeu se déroulait devant le but aurillacois et Rayan Fontaine, servi par Adem Moussaoui, d'un tir dans un angle fermé aggravait le score. (ASSE-AFCA : 2-0, 7ème)La domination verte ne se relâchait pas : sur un corner, la reprise de la tête de Raphaël Moser était détournée par le gardien (17ème), un coup-franc de Lenny Nebout, tiré à ras de terre, était repoussé par le portier cantalou et la reprise de Noah Fontaine ne trouvait pas le cadre (18ème), un tir de loin de Dixon Ahamadi était une nouvelle fois détourné (22ème). Entre temps, une première incursion aurillacoise était ponctuée par un corner, mais la reprise de la tête n,'inquiétait pas Ilan Clapeyron.  Les Verts allaient de nouveau trouver la faille : à la suite d'une combinaison avec Noah Fontaine, Hugo Durin était trouvé dans un petit espace et sa frappe croisée du gauche faisait mouche. (ASSE-AFCA : 3-0, 24ème).Dès la remise en jeu, le défenseur central Idris Balta s'avançait, plaçait un tir qui rebondissait devant le but et trompait le gardien adverse. (ASSE-AFCA : 4-0, 25ème).A la 30ème minute, suite à un centre de Raphaël Moser, Hugo Durin remisait sur Joris Rochette (photo), mais la reprise de ce dernier était contrée. Aurillac réagissait timidement à la 38ème et sur un tir venu de loin, Ilan Clapeyron se détendait bien. C'était un petit intermède au milieu de la domination stéphanoise qui ne se démentait pas : un coup-franc de Rayan Fontaine trouvait la tête de Dixon Ahamadi, mais le gardien adverse captait le cuir (40ème), une frappe lointaine de Joris Rochette s'écrasait sur l'équerre du but cantalou (43ème), sur une combinaison côté gauche, le tir de Raphaël Moser dans un angle fermé frôlait la transversale (44ème), et, enfin à la 45ème, un tir dévié de Joris Rochette, manquait de tromper le gardien. La mi-temps était sifflée sur ces entrefaites. Le score de 4 à 0 illustrait la mainmise stéphanoise.

Le second acte repartait avec la même physionomie. A la 50ème une subtile combinaison Joris Rochette - Hugo Durin butait sur le gardien. A la 52ème, Joris Rochette repiquait au centre et sa frappe du gauche passait à côté. La minute suivante Hugo Durin alertait Rayan Fontaine et le centre de ce dernier trouvait la tête de son frère Noah, mais sa reprise était détournée en corner, corner sur lequel la tête de Dixon Ahamadi ne trouvait pas le cadre. A la 55ème, Rayan Fontaine était fauché à l'entrée de la surface et le coup-franc de Raphaël Moser s'écrasait sur la transversale aurillacoise. A force d'appuyer, les Verts allaient trouver la faille : une frappe de 25 mètres de Dixon Ahamadi était détournée par le gardien et sur le corner qui suivait Rayan Fontaine trouvait la tête d'Hugo Durin. (ASSE-AFCA : 5-0, 56ème) A la 62ème, Hugo Durin servait latéralement Lenny Nebout mais la frappe de ce dernier était stoppée par le gardien. Servi par une passe verticale d'Idris Balta, Kaïs Boukerma voyait son tir détourné par le portier aurillacois (65ème). A la 69ème, Rayan Fontaine trouvait Hugo Durin dans le dos de la défense et ce dernier concluait du droit. (ASSE-AFCA : 6-0, 69ème).Peu après, Hugo Durin, alerté par Joris Rochette, partait de la ligne médiane, prenait de vitesse la défense adverse et s'en allait marquer du droit. (ASSE-AFCA : 7-0, 72ème).Joris Rochette faisait un festival côté droit et son centre en retrait trouvait Riad Moutae qui  parachevait cette belle action. (ASSE-AFCA : 8-0, 76ème).Enfin, alors qu'il restait une dizaine de minutes à jouer, une belle passe cachée de Lenny Nebout pour Hugo Durin permettait à ce dernier de conclure d'une frappe décroisée entre le gardien et son poteau. C'était son 6ème but de l'après-midi ! (ASSE-AFCA : 9-0, 81ème). Le match à sens unique se terminait sur ce score fleuve qui reflétait bien la sérieuse prestation des jeunes Verts.

La composition : Clapeyron - R.Fontaine, Ahamadi, Balta, Moser - Evaristo, Rochette, Moussaoui (Boukerma, 60ème)- Nebout, Durin, N.Fontaine (Moutae, 60ème).

La réaction de Kevin de Jesus : "Satisfait du match ? Certes, mais mon but c'est de voir des comportements qui progressent, qui avancent vers ce que j'exige des jeunes. A la mi-temps, le résultat semblait acquis, mais j'ai demandé à mes joueurs de continuer à trouver des solutions pour déséquilibrer l'équipe adverse, de varier les combinaisons pour arriver à cet objectif, en diversifiant les circuits, en impliquant toute l'équipe dans cette recherche, défense y compris, par les montées des excentrés dans leur couloir, des centraux dans l'axe pour tenter des frappes de loin. J'ai apprécié le sérieux des joueurs qui sont restés concentrés, sans s'enflammer, en respectant l'adversaire. Cet esprit-là est important."

#2401. PSV back on top of Eredivisie as Feyenoord slump in Heerenveen

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

PSV returned to the top of the Eredivisie with a thumping 5-2 win over Cambuur Leeuwarden as previous leaders Feyenoord lost a seven-goal thriller against the other Frisian club, Heerenveen.

It took just 46 seconds for PSV to get off the mark as Sven Mijnans headed in unmarked.

The midfielder added a second after 15 minutes and completed his hat-trick with a free-kick in the 80th minute to make the score 4-2, just as Cambuur were threatening a comeback.

Feyenoord’s dip in form continued as they let a two-goal lead slip at Heerenveen. The Rotterdammers looked to be in control going into the break with a trademark drilled shot by Anis Hadj Moussa and a penalty by Nacho Ferri.

But Maas Willemsen bundled in the ball from a corner on the stroke of half-time, before Ringo Meerveld came on for the second half and scored a hat-trick as Feyenoord’s defence crumbled under pressure.

“In the matches when we played well I saw a team that fought for each other,” Feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst said after the game. “Mentally strong, kept running even when we didn’t have the ball. That’s our strength. When we don’t do that we’re a lesser team.”

Mexx Meerdink scored a hotly contested late penalty to settle a tempestuous game in Alkmaar as AZ came back from 3-1 down against Groningen to claim their first win in five matches.

Goalkeeper Etienne Vaessen was given a second yellow card for protesting too hard against the decision to penalise him for upending Ayoub Oufkir. Once the commotion died down Meerdink, who had missed from the spot against Vaessen earlier in the second half, made no mistake against substitute goalkeeper Lovro Stubljar.

Ajax missed the chance to take over top spot at Twente as their former striker Wout Weghorst scored a last-minute penalty to rescue a point for the home side.

Ajax had been 2-0 up with a bullet header by their giant striker Tolu Arokodare and a long-range strike by Rayane Bounida, before an own goal by Dies Janse brought the visitors back into the game.

Fortuna Sittard also had to settle for a point against Telstar after going 2-0 up thanks to a bizarre own goal by Sem Valk. The defender’s sliced clearance looped over the head of Ronald Koeman Junior as the goalkeeper tried to head it away rather than risk being penalised for handling a backpass.

Goals just before half-time by Abdelnour Soualhia and Patrick Brouwer brought Telstar back into the game, but neither side was able to find a winner after the break.

That result allowed ADO, under the guidance of interim coach Levi Schwiebbe, to close the gap on 16th-placed Telstar to one point with a 3-1 win against Sparta, while bottom Willem II collected their third point of the season at home to PEC Zwolle.

#2399. Lazzari nel post: "Punto preziosissimo. Gattuso? Ci ha ridato gioia e adrenalina"

Manuel Lazzari ha rilasciato delle dichiarazioni ai microfoni di LSC e Dazn poco dopo il fischio finale di Napoli-Lazio

Manuel Lazzari ha rilasciato delle dichiarazioni ai microfoni di LSC e Dazn poco dopo il fischio finale di Napoli-Lazio.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Questo punto ce lo prendiamo volentieri, è importantissimo perché abbiamo disputato un primo tempo importante e potevamo fare qualche gol in più. Nel secondo tempo il Napoli è cresciuto, sapevamo che venivamo in un campo difficile sapevamo che per loro era “l’ultima spiaggia” quindi ce lo prendiamo volentieri.

Abbiamo fatto un inizio di stagione incredibile, nessuno se lo aspettava e sin dal primo giorno il mister ci ha dato tante idee. Siamo cresciuti molto, è una gioia andare tutti i giorni a Formello ad allenarci. Dobbiamo seguire il mister e continuare così.

Il mister ha ridato gioia, adrenalina e un calcio completamente diverso rispetto allo scorso anno. Il gruppo lo ha seguito sin da subito, dopo 11 partite la risposta la squadra l’ha data e ora continuiamo così.

Penso che abbiamo approcciato alla partita in maniera meravigliosa, abbiamo fatto un grande primo tempo con diverse occasioni da gol e siamo riusciti a sbloccarla. Nel secondo tempo loro sono cresciuti, verso la metà della ripresa ci siamo equilibrati e a 10 minuti dalla fine volevamo tornare a casa con una vittoria ma venire a Napoli e sapere che per loro era l’ultima spiaggia, è un punto preziosissimo.

Questo punto ce lo prediamo alla grande perché 9 vittorie e 2 pareggi, nessuno se lo sarebbe aspettato a inizio stagione. Campo difficile, per loro era la gara della vita. Abbiamo fatto un grandissimo primo tempo, nel secondo loro sono cresciuti e poi da metà del secondo tempo diamo riusciti a riequilibrare la sfida. Punto veramente importante.

Il mister quest’anno è stato un fenomeno, ha portato allegria, gioia, voglia di essere protagonisti, di attaccare. Ha portato tante idee nuove e tutti i giocatori sia chi gioca che chi gioca meno è felice di allenasi oggi giorno. Il mister ha creato un gran gruppo, dobbiamo solo continuare a seguirlo.

Un grandissimo saluto ai tifosi, ieri è stato magnifico in stazione e speriamo di rivederli presto.
